subject: paper:noreika-2013
quote: The review demonstrates that ADHD patients are consistently impaired in three major timing domains, in motor timing, perceptual timing and temporal foresight, comprising several timeframes spanning milliseconds, seconds, minutes and longer intervals up to years.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). An integrative review's summary that timing impairment in ADHD is consistent across domains and timescales — the core empirical support.

subject: paper:toplak-2006
quote: While further replication is needed, growing evidence links ADHD to problems in several aspects of temporal information processing, including duration discrimination, duration reproduction, and finger tapping.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Names the specific temporal-processing tasks impaired in ADHD (the mechanism's content) while explicitly flagging that the evidence still needs replication — the caveat carried into the marker tension.

subject: paper:ptacek-2019
quote: individuals with ADHD have difficulties in time estimation and discrimination activities as well as having the feeling that time is passing by without them being able to complete tasks accurately and well.
rationale: Verbatim from the open-access Med Sci Monit review. Links the measured estimation/discrimination deficits to the lived 'time blindness' experience.

subject: paper:ptacek-2019
quote: This review summarizes recent research on the perception of time in ADHD and proposes that this symptom is a possible diagnostic characteristic.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. States the diagnostic-marker proposal explicitly; medium confidence because it is the authors' proposal, and timing deficits are not specific to ADHD (see the tension).
